_comment: One entry per documented moment. `seconds` is where playback should start, backed up a few seconds so the viewer hears the lead-in. `videoDate`, when present and different from `date`, means the footage comes from a later meeting that recounts the event rather than from the event itself, and the page says so. `note` adds a caveat shown to the reader. Entries with no `seconds` are ones the meeting video does not let us locate; the page states what happened and why it is not on tape. Quotes from automatic captions are cleaned for punctuation only and checked against the audio.

moments.title: Fourteen actions, one vote — on a document Mayor Bianca had not seen
moments.quote: I did not have the benefit of receiving these ahead of the meeting. I note there are 14 motions. Normally with a motion there are individual seconds after a motion is made, and then a vote, so I'm hoping that's the intent. The Mayor and Council recently approved as one of our core values transparency. So I hope it's the intent with these, since they didn't get any public notice, that not only will they be read but that they will be acted upon in accordance with the way this document is structured — individually.
moments.speaker: Mayor Bianca Motley Broom, asking for fourteen separate votes

clips.label: The answer: one vote
clips.quote: This item is going to be voted on as one single consent agenda item. Now, of course, we read the items individually, but we're going to vote on them all together. Not going to do 14 votes or whatever.
clips.speaker: Councilman Joe Carn
clips.gloss: Carn answers her directly. The reading will be item by item; the vote will not be. That distinction is the whole design — the public hears fourteen things, the record shows one decision.

clips.label: Mayor Bianca names the item and asks the city attorney
clips.quote: It seems to me that this is very diverse subjects. Some seem to suggest rules and procedures for conducting a meeting, but then there are others that I would suggest effect changes [to] the form of government — such as the item that deals with the council having the ability to determine terminations of city employees. So I will tell you, if that's voted on along with other more procedural items, I have deep concerns.
clips.speaker: Mayor Bianca Motley Broom, to City Attorney Winston Denmark
clips.gloss: She turns to the lawyer because she knows the bundling is the problem, and she points at the one motion that proves it. This is her trying to stop it through the process rather than by objecting after the fact.

clips.label: The question is never answered
clips.quote: My understanding is that there's nothing in here that's a substantial change to form of government at all. / I disagree. / Well, that's why we have a city attorney. / [reading] I'm reading them all, sir. We're doing them collectively, we're voting collectively.
clips.speaker: Councilman Joe Carn, then Mayor Bianca, then Carn again
clips.gloss: Watch who answers. She asked the city attorney a legal question; Carn responds instead, and the attorney never speaks. She says she disagrees, Carn says that's why we have a city attorney, and the reading starts anyway. The question stays open to this day.

clips.label: Motion three, eleven seconds later
clips.quote: While presiding over the deliberations of the city council in accordance with the charter, the mayor shall be prohibited from commenting or expressing opinions on the matters being discussed.
clips.speaker: Read into the record as motion three
clips.gloss: Now you know what was inside the bundle she was trying to slow down. Motion three arrives in the middle of a list, read at the same pace as the rest, and it removes her voice from every debate that follows.

moments.title: Mayor Bianca is barred from commenting
moments.quote: While presiding over the deliberations of the city council in accordance with the charter, the mayor shall be prohibited from commenting or expressing opinions on the matters being discussed.
moments.speaker: Read into the record as motion three

moments.title: Mayor Bianca states the objection on the record
moments.quote: Motion three, in regard to this omnibus motion that was dealt with at our meeting, among others, infringes my rights under the First Amendment of the US Constitution to participate in these meetings. As a duly elected official, the charter vested me the power to preside over the meetings of this governing body, and the omnibus motion seeks to strip those duties and responsibilities from the office of the mayor.
moments.speaker: Mayor Bianca Motley Broom

moments.title: The legislative assistants are reassigned
moments.quote: In terms of legislative assistants reorganization, we're going to have assistants report directly to council and mayor, and administratively to the office of the city manager.
moments.speaker: Councilman Joe Carn, reading the amended omnibus

moments.title: Ordinance 2024-01 adopted
moments.quote: I would like to make a comment and then entertain— / Point of order. While you're presiding you may not make a comment. The chair cannot make a comment. So when it's time to vote, you can hand the gavel back to the mayor and then she'll call for a vote, or you make comment at that time once she's presiding once more.
moments.speaker: Mayor Pro Tem, then a council member raising the point of order

moments.title: All four refuse to take it
moments.quote: I would turn those over to Council member Carn. / No, you will not.
moments.speaker: Mayor Bianca, then Councilman Joe Carn

clips.label: Down the line
clips.quote: Council member Arnold, I will pass the gavel to you. / I decline. / Council member McKenzie, I will pass the— / I decline, because I'm the one that's made the motion, and I'm making a motion with discussion, so I'm unable to do that.
clips.speaker: Mayor Bianca, then Councilwoman Tracy Arnold, then Councilwoman Jamelle McKenzie
clips.gloss: She keeps going down the line anyway. Arnold refuses. McKenzie refuses and explains that she made the motion, so she can't preside. The Mayor Pro Tem is following the guidance the attorney just gave, and every seat after him does the same. Nobody has to argue with her. They simply decline, and she stays in the chair, unable to speak.

moments.note: The meeting was called to consider rescinding the Council's termination of City Manager Stanley Hawthorne. That is the conversation Mayor Bianca was asking to speak to.

moments.title: Mayor Bianca tries to use the way out the rule describes
moments.quote: Has the Mayor Pro Tem accepted the gavel? / I decline.
moments.speaker: Mayor Bianca, then Mayor Pro Tem Roderick Gay

clips.label: Why Mayor Bianca is handing it off
clips.quote: I've relinquished presiding duties to the Mayor Pro Tem, as I wish to speak to this conversation. / The Mayor Pro Tem may elect not to assume the gavel. / I'd like not to assume the gavel at this time.
clips.speaker: Mayor Bianca, an unidentified voice, then the Mayor Pro Tem
clips.gloss: She explains herself: she is stepping down from the chair only so she can speak, exactly as they told the Mayor Pro Tem to do six days earlier. Then a voice cuts in to remind him he doesn't have to take it — and he immediately doesn't.

clips.label: Mayor Bianca asks the city attorney whether she may speak at all
clips.quote: Mr. Denmark — in regard to my ability to speak when I am not presiding over these meetings, I wish to do that. Is that permissible, or am I prohibited from speaking altogether?
clips.speaker: Mayor Bianca Motley Broom
clips.gloss: She has run out of options at the table, so she asks the lawyer in the room whether she is allowed to speak at all. Listen to how carefully she asks it. She is not arguing; she is trying to find out what is left.

clips.label: The city attorney confirms the refusal is theirs to make
clips.quote: You could pass the gavel to the Mayor Pro Tem or colleague if they were inclined to accept — but it's their decision. And if [you] wish to participate in discussions, that would be inconsistent with the ordinance that the council passed.
clips.speaker: City Attorney Winston Denmark
clips.gloss: This is the answer that settles it. The way out exists, but only a colleague can open it, and he says plainly that the choice is theirs. From this point everyone in the room knows that refusing the gavel is enough to keep her silent.

moments.note: A voice tells the Mayor Pro Tem he may decline, immediately before he declines a second time. The phrasing is a lawyer's, but automatic captions carry no speaker labels, so this page does not put a name to it. Denmark's formal answer is attributed because Mayor Bianca addresses him by name first.

moments.title: Special meetings no longer Mayor Bianca's call
moments.quote: Changing the requirement for special meetings removes authority from the mayor to call special meetings, and then decreases the number required from four to three. I don't think this is a good idea. Special meetings infer that there is urgency. It also removes a critical component of feedback from the public — council is taking actions and the public doesn't have a voice in that regard.
moments.speaker: Mayor Bianca Motley Broom

moments.title: Questions to staff ruled out of order
moments.quote: Point of order — we're out of order here, this is the city manager's report. / I had a question for him during his report. We haven't moved on to the next item yet. So, sir, I do have questions.
moments.speaker: A council member, then Mayor Bianca Motley Broom

moments.title: Federal delegation lead reassigned
moments.note: The federal delegation is discussed at several points in the 3h meeting, but no single moment states the reassignment plainly enough to quote. Needs a watch-through of 1:16:00-1:22:00.

moments.title: Budget hearings taken off the air
moments.quote: That's probably where the best — would be the better place to do it. / Are you making a motion to not televise the budget hearings? / I am.
moments.speaker: The chair, confirming the motion with its maker

moments.title: Closing remarks capped at five minutes
moments.note: The 4h36m meeting is captioned, but the captioner drops most of the late-agenda procedural exchange where this vote happened. The ordinance text is the better citation here; the video is confirmation, not the primary source.

moments.title: A resident livestreams the budget hearing
moments.note: No city video exists. The Council had voted not to stream these hearings. The only recording was the resident's phone.

moments.title: Comment moved to the end of the agenda, for one night
moments.note: Only 1h19m across two uploads for a meeting that ran longer, and the agenda discussion isn't in the captioned portion. Likely a partial upload.

moments.title: Council votes Mayor Bianca out of order for a question
moments.quote: You're discussing items, Mayor, which is out of order of how we do things. And so actually doing a second one would be out of order as well.
moments.speaker: Councilwoman Jamelle McKenzie

moments.title: Censure, and the room is cleared
moments.note: The August 9 meeting is posted but carries no captions, so the moment cannot be located inside it by transcript. This is the next regular meeting, August 19, where a television report on the cleared gallery was played into the record. A contemporaneous account, not footage of the clearing.
moments.quote: The Georgia attorney general's office is demanding answers from College Park officials after the gallery was cleared by police during a specially called meeting last Friday. Two people were led away in handcuffs as the interim city manager told police to eject the residents from the room. The meeting was held to censure Mayor Bianca Motley Broom for what the city council says was ongoing disruptive behavior.
moments.speaker: A television news report, played into the record

moments.title: Mayor Bianca speaks from the public podium
moments.note: The meeting is captioned and Mayor Bianca is audible throughout, but the captions never render the line where she gives her name and address at the podium. Needs a watch-through.

moments.title: Thirty minutes for the room, six for everyone else
moments.quote: Council member McKenzie, what was your motion? / The motion was that we would adhere to 30 minutes here for in-person comments and 6 minutes for email comments. / What was happening is email comments weren't getting read at all, so we said we would make sure that we would give 6 minutes for email comments.
moments.speaker: Mayor Bianca, then Councilwoman Jamelle McKenzie
moments.note: Carn voted in favor, Gay abstained.

clips.label: Six minutes, inside the thirty-six
clips.quote: The timer is 36 minutes — does that include the six minutes for email? / Yes ma'am, I believe it does include the six minutes. The 36 minutes total.
clips.speaker: A council member, then the chair
clips.gloss: The clarification is the part that matters. A resident asks whether the six minutes are on top of the thirty-six or inside them. Inside. So the guarantee for everyone who couldn't attend comes out of the same clock as everyone who did.

moments.title: Fifteen minutes per topic
moments.note: The full 2h53m meeting is posted, but this upload carries no auto-captions at all, so the moment can't be located by transcript search. Needs a watch-through.

moments.title: Motion to override the chair
moments.note: Five uploads exist for this date and none of them carries captions. Needs a watch-through of the 2h02m council meeting.

moments.title: A resident told to step outside
moments.note: Two problems. Only 5 minutes of a full regular session was posted, and that upload has no captions. This is the thinnest spot in the city's record for any date on this timeline.

moments.title: Housing protester escorted out
moments.note: Captions exist for the 3h40m meeting, but nothing matching a removal appears in them. Either the exchange was off-mic or the captioner dropped it. Needs a watch-through.

moments.title: Police at the podium
moments.quote: No, no, this isn't me. This is the guy that they're hiring, sir. This is Councilwoman McKenzie and Joe Carn. They want to spend $40,000. / Hold on, Chief. Chief, hold on. Mr. James — we won't allow profanity to be played.
moments.speaker: A resident at the podium, then the chair

clips.label: What he was not allowed to play
clips.quote: It is odd to me that the city would finance the voice that I was just playing for you — and an opportunity not to run against their own person. But I can't play his words in here.
clips.speaker: Mose James IV, at the podium
clips.gloss: He keeps his composure and makes the point without the tape: the city is considering paying this man to speak for it. He is not allowed to let the room hear what that voice actually sounds like.

clips.label: What was on the recording
clips.quote: I was kind enough to actually bleep out over 30 curse words that you're going to hear in the next three and a half minutes from the person that this council has decided to be the voice piece of College Park. You'll go on to hear him repeatedly refer to the mayor as a B—
clips.speaker: Mose James IV, at the podium
clips.gloss: Here is what was on the recording, described rather than played. He had already bleeped more than thirty obscenities before bringing it into the chamber. The council still would not hear it — while considering a contract with the person who said it.

photo.alt: Three College Park police officers standing at the public comment podium beside Mose James IV as he speaks into the microphone
photo.caption: Three officers at the public comment podium, September 2, 2025. He is still inside his three minutes.

moments.title: A resident names the pattern from the podium
moments.quote: The role of the mayor is not ceremonial. The mayor is elected citywide and trusted by residents to represent their interests. When council actively blocks her from adding items, it's not simply silencing one official. It's cutting off an avenue for the public's concerns to be heard and addressed through their elected representative. We've seen a pattern of silencing the mayor, limiting transparency, and rushing initiatives without proper vetting. This isn't governance that's rooted in accountability. This is governance that's just rooted in control.
moments.speaker: A resident, during public comment

moments.title: Posted minutes become action-only
moments.quote: Is there a motion to approve the regular session minutes from October 20th? / Motion. / Thank you, Council Member Carn. Is there a second? / Second.
moments.speaker: The chair, moving the minutes
moments.note: Nothing is said aloud about the format changing. You can see it by comparing the documents: the minutes approved from this night forward record actions only, where earlier sets carried the discussion speaker by speaker. The clip fixes the date; the paperwork is the proof.

moments.title: Yielding time, while it was still allowed
moments.quote: Mario Malcolm also waives his time. So that'll be six additional minutes.
moments.speaker: The chair, counting yielded time
moments.note: Kept here as the before picture. Residents pooled their minutes as a matter of routine in November 2025. In August 2026 the council prohibited it.

moments.title: The 30-minute cap, enforced
moments.quote: I would like to address the public. The in-person public comment is allowed for 30 minutes and we have exhausted the 30 minute time. The remainder of the six minutes is for emailed public comments.
moments.speaker: Mayor Bianca Motley Broom, announcing the cutoff
moments.note: The cap in operation. Everyone still waiting to speak in the room is done, with the balance of the period going to email.

moments.title: Resolution 2025-44 ends email comment
moments.quote: Approve a resolution regarding City of College Park public comment policy. This item is sponsored by city attorney.
moments.speaker: Clerk, reading Resolution 2025-44

moments.title: Ordinance 2026-12 and the 60-minute cap
moments.quote: Someone make [a motion] for 60 minutes, please. We need someone to make a motion that we can cut off the public hearing at 60 minutes.
moments.speaker: The chair, soliciting the motion

moments.title: Yielding time prohibited
moments.note: The 1h30m meeting is posted without captions. Needs a watch-through.

moments.title: Public hearing capped at 30 minutes
moments.note: A single 5h45m upload with no captions. The longest meeting on the timeline and the hardest to search.

moments.title: A limit on the Council dies for lack of a second
moments.quote: Consideration of action to approve a resolution for the establishment of 9:30 p.m. end time for regular business and 3 minute comment limit per elected official. This item is council-sponsored by Councilwoman Tracy Arnold. / Is there a motion? / [seven seconds of silence] / Motion dies for lack of a second.
moments.speaker: City Clerk reading the item, then the chair
moments.note: Arnold sponsored the item and no colleague would second it, so this particular restriction never took effect. The seven seconds of silence are the record.
